questions.prompt: A public booking page is readable in a browser. What does that visibility authorize in this course?

options.text: Reading the public page only; active testing still needs specific owner authorization
Collecting production reservations
Testing accounts behind the page
Disrupting the service for education

questions.explanation: Public readability does not authorize probes, account tests, data collection or disruption; the approved exercise uses synthetic records.

questions.prompt: Which brief defines a usable boundary for the Harbor Library tabletop?

options.text: Test the library until satisfied
Name the owner, synthetic materials, permitted actions, excluded systems, time, stop rule and report recipient
Use any available resident records
Skip a stop rule because the exercise is educational

questions.explanation: The one-page brief makes scope and authority reviewable before practice starts, including exclusions and a defined exit.

questions.prompt: Which item remains outside the approved paper exercise even if it might answer a learner's question?

options.text: Two invented booking rows
An invented 09:00 printout
A role-play front-desk decision
A real booking account or production website

questions.explanation: The authorization brief explicitly excludes real accounts, residents, the live booking page and production data.

questions.prompt: For the stale-printout question, which data choice follows the minimization rule?

options.text: Remove times and retain only the resident name
Keep all resident fields in case they become useful
Retain booking ID, room, start and creation times; remove resident name and phone
Copy credentials to make the sample reproducible

questions.explanation: The exercise needs timing and room evidence, not personal identifiers. Each retained field should serve the learning question.

questions.prompt: Under the stated fixed 09:00 snapshot assumption, which invented booking can the printout include?

options.text: Neither booking because the page later failed
Both bookings because they are confirmed
Only SYN-002 because it is later
SYN-001 created at 08:20, but not SYN-002 created at 10:05

questions.explanation: A fixed 09:00 copy can contain the earlier row but not a row created at 10:05; this is an explicit exercise assumption.

questions.prompt: A sample sheet unexpectedly contains a real patron's name. What should participants do?

options.text: Pause the exercise, protect the sheet and ask the designated owner for direction
Delete it without telling the owner
Circulate the sheet for realism
Continue until the scheduled end

questions.explanation: A real name triggers the prewritten stop condition; the team should avoid further circulation and follow the owner's process.

questions.prompt: Which report sentence is calibrated to the paper exercise?

options.text: The real library suffered a critical breach
The synthetic 09:00 copy omitted a later invented booking; current real-world procedure was not tested
All staff always rely on stale printouts
The outage was caused by a compromised account

questions.explanation: The record supports a gap in the synthetic comparison and a possible procedure concern, not a production breach or universal claim.

questions.prompt: What should the second tabletop round measure after introducing the pending-queue rule?

options.text: Whether an unknown live system can be penetrated
Whether the worker avoids confirming a later request from the stale printout
Whether every future outage will be harmless
Whether the contact list can be exported

questions.explanation: The exercise can observe a role-play decision difference. A single synthetic session cannot establish reliability in all settings.

questions.prompt: A participant proposes opening the real site halfway through the paper exercise. What is the next authorized step?

options.text: Pause the live proposal and ask the owner while preserving an offline path
Open it quickly before the owner notices
Treat a public URL as standing permission
Rewrite the scope after completing the test

questions.explanation: The prewritten boundary forbids live checks; the owner decides whether a different approved action is needed.

questions.prompt: How does a real incident evidence duty differ from this classroom exercise?

options.text: Real records should always be deleted to minimize data
The tabletop authorizes production collection
Classroom inputs start synthetic; real incident evidence follows the organization's approved retention process
Personal data is required to make a lesson credible

questions.explanation: The classroom can avoid personal data from the start, while real incident records may have preservation obligations under an approved process.
